title: Universal Adaptive Proximal Gradient Methods via Gradient Mapping Accumulation
claim: The adaptive method converges across a wide range of hyperparameter settings, while the fixed-step baseline only converges when its step size is well tuned.
layout: 3 panels in a row, log-log convergence plots, shared axes, (a)(b)(c) labels
description: Three side-by-side log-log line plots. They show the gradient mapping norm ||G(x)|| on the y-axis, from 1e0 down to 1e-10, against iterations on the x-axis, from 1e0 to 1e4. Panel (a) is Algorithm 1 and panel (b) is Algorithm 2. Each has curves for three values of the parameter eta (1, 10, 100) in blue, orange and green. Panel (c) is plain proximal gradient (PG) with step sizes alpha = 0.1/L, 1/L and 10/L, using the same colors with triangle markers. In (a), the eta=100 curve oscillates heavily before dropping sharply near 5e3 iterations. In (b), all three curves decrease steadily. In (c), the 10/L curve stalls on a plateau and the 0.1/L curve decreases slowly. Only the 1/L curve drops steeply. The eye goes to the orange curve falling steeply and to the noisy green curve.
caption: Evolution of ∥G(x)∥for solving the nonconvex SVM problem (6.1) on the MNIST dataset in the deterministic setting.
abstract: We propose an adaptive proximal gradient method for minimizing the sum of two functions, where one is a simple convex function, and the other belongs to one of the three classes: nonconvex smooth, convex nonsmooth, or convex smooth. The key feature of the method is an adaptive step size that accumulates historical gradient mapping norms in the denominator. Without any modification or knowledge of problem parameters, the method converges across all three problem classes under mild bounded-iterates and bounded-variance assumptions, with rates matching those of the proximal gradient method up to logarithmic factors, in both deterministic and stochastic settings. For the convex setting, we further propose an accelerated variant. It retains a similar near-optimal convergence rate for the nonsmooth case and achieves an improved rate of order $\widetilde{O}\big(1/t^2 + Ï/\sqrt{t}\big)$ for the smooth case, which is optimal up to logarithmic factors. Notably, we develop new techniques for controlling the effect of stochastic noise, which are applicable across all three problem classes in the stochastic setting and enable a simplified analysis.
